title: Transport Corporation of India Ltd - 532349 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: TCI Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew ~9% (24th straight quarter of growth) while standalone profit turned slightly negative on lower JV dividends and bunker costs.
summary.overview: Management reported 9% consolidated top-line growth and 7% standalone growth for Q1 FY27, with the freight business up 10-11%. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 1.6% and PAT slightly negative, largely because JV dividend income was lower; consolidated EBITDA was about 5%. Seaways margins were flat as bunker prices rose to around Rs 86,000/ton, partly offset by rate increases; the Concor JV grew about 88% and Cold Chain about 48%. Management guided supply chain to 12-15% growth and freight to 10-12%, with capex of Rs 550-600 crore for FY27 (Rs 167 crore spent in Q1).

segments.name: Supply chain (standalone)
segments.commentary: Growth moderate against a high base; EBITDA margin slightly improved but EBIT flat. Management expects 12-15% top-line growth for FY27, pick-up in H2 from new contracts and diesel pass-through bills.

segments.name: Freight
segments.commentary: Top line up ~10-11% with slight margin improvement; 10 of planned 30 new branches opened in Q1. FY27 guidance 10-12% growth with higher profitability.

segments.name: Seaways
segments.commentary: Revenue up on pricing with similar voyages (one ship dry-docked); margins flat. Bunker prices at ~Rs 86,000/ton; Q2 EBITDA guided at 25-30%, and new ships expected Sept-Oct and Oct-Nov.

segments.name: Concor JV
segments.commentary: Grew ~88% per management; revenue moderated vs last quarter per Q&A. Rail shift from road limited due to lean season and rail congestion.

segments.name: Cold Chain JV
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~48% from contracts won in Q3-Q4 FY26; still small in quantum.

segments.name: Trans System JV (Toyota-linked, Mitsui partner)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~11.5%, but margin fell to ~9% from 14-15% on pricing pressure and production cuts; profit run-rate down to ~Rs 30 crore from Rs 40-42 crore. Management sees ~10% margin as reasonable.

guidance_outlook: Supply chain revenue growth 12-15% for FY27, with pick-up expected from Q2 onwards.
Freight revenue growth 10-12% for FY27 with higher profitability year on year.
Seaways Q2 EBITDA margin guided at 25-30%; FY27 Seaways EBITDA may rise on higher depreciation from new ships, but profitability may subdue for one or two quarters after induction.

FY27 capex budget Rs 550-600 crore (management estimate Rs 500-600 crore): ~Rs 237 crore on ships, ~Rs 100 crore warehouses, ~Rs 120 crore trucks and rakes, ~Rs 100 crore warehousing equipment and IT.
JV dividend payout expected similar to last year; not expected to rise in the next year or two due to capex.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex Rs 167 crore against FY26 total of ~Rs 370 crore.
Two new ships expected in Sept-end and Oct-Nov 2026; a third ship under exploration with advance payment possible.
Dry dock: one ship completed already; one scheduled for late March 2027; dry-dock duration 25-35 days.
Freight network: 30 new branches planned for FY27, 10 opened in Q1.
Supply chain: 'trucks being added based on new contracts'; 624 rakes handled in Q1, flat YoY; 67 yards managed; three owned rakes.
demand_pricing: Auto sector accounts for ~75-80% of supply chain business; management says auto demand robust but some customers slowed in Q1 as Q4 pipeline inventory was delivered.
Bunker prices rose sharply from late Feb-March 2026 on Middle East crisis; ranged ~Rs 72,000-1,05,000/ton in recent weeks; fuel discounts no longer available.
Diesel price up ~6-7%; management estimates pass-through impact of 1-2% of revenue, with contract customers lagging.
Rail congestion and monsoon/lean season limited shift from road to rail; containers backlog ~10,000-12,000 at JNPT.
Trans System pricing pressure and production cuts at Japanese OEM clients; some low-priced business not renewed.

qa_highlights.question: Can supply chain reach 12-15% growth in H2 and how much diesel-linked price growth came in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites pipeline and new contracts from H2, plus supplementary diesel bills from mid-May; Q1 diesel-linked benefit was minimal, mostly volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Seaways profitability with bunker volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Bunker prices are volatile; Q2 EBITDA expected at 25-30%. New ships take 4-6 months to reach full utilisation; breakeven timing not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Why is freight profit not improving despite the auto recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Some customers were served from Q4 pipeline inventory; longer-haul replenishment expected in subsequent quarters; mix shift and 30 new branches to drive margin, a slow process.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable days and capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital days ~55-56; some pressure expected from rate hikes but credit policies in place. FY27 capex mainly ships, trucks/rakes, warehouses.

qa_highlights.question: Margin impact of LTL mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: LTL gross margin ~20% vs FTL ~10%; mix shift from ~35-37% to ~40% is gradual, adding a few basis points per 1% shift.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Trans System margins fall and what is the JV earnings outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment in expansion, pricing pressure and lost low-priced business; ~10% margin seen as reasonable. JV profitability guided similar to last year; Toyota plant at Aurangabad to need investment next fiscal.

risks_watch: Bunker price volatility tied to Middle East hostilities could compress Seaways margins in Q2.
Supply chain growth must accelerate to 12-15% in H2 from a moderate Q1; auto customer demand timing uncertain.
Standalone PAT turned slightly negative; JV dividend income lower, affecting profit visibility.
Trans System margin decline (to ~9%) and falling profit contribution.
Working capital pressure from rate hikes; receivable days ~55-56.
Labour shortages and cost pressure in warehousing after LPG disruption; possible shutdown of gas-hit customers.
key_quotes: So, we do expect the growth to pick up in the latter half of the year.
So, it is very unpredictable and very difficult to give you a basic margin, basic changes.

The expectation is that we are cautiously optimistic. There is some uncertainty because of the Middle East, but with the possibility of increased sales during the festival season, we are seeing that restocking starting, and we do expect that to continue in the next few months.
I do not think we'll get back to that 11 -12% type of range because that seems to be always a little bit on the higher side. Probably, I think about 10% is more reasonable.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic overall, with management confident on the H2 supply-chain pipeline and freight margin mix, but evasive on bunker-driven Seaways margins and Trans System profitability, where it repeatedly said outcomes are unpredictable. Guidance is held (supply chain 12-15%, freight 10-12%) even as Q1 supply-chain growth was moderate and standalone PAT turned slightly negative.
